questions.stem: Which of the following is an objective of Vendor Risk Management? (Choose two.)

options.text: To help vendors improve their security posture and preparedness
To assess and manage the risk from interactions with vendors and third parties
To help negotiate the best possible price for a product or service from the vendor
To verify that vendors have adequate measures and processes in place to ensure profitability of vendor

questions.explanation: Vendor Risk Management has two core objectives: assessing and managing risk from vendor/third-party interactions (B), and helping vendors improve their security posture and preparedness through issue remediation and continuous assessment (A). Negotiating prices (C) is procurement, not VRM. Ensuring vendor profitability (D) is irrelevant to risk management.

questions.stem: The Vendor records are stored in which table?
questions.explanation: Vendor records in ServiceNow are stored in the Company [core_company] table with a vendor=true flag. The Company table holds all organizational entities including vendors, partners, and customers. The sys_user table stores individual contacts, not vendor entities. Department and Task tables serve entirely different purposes.

questions.stem: Internal roles include: (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Internal roles are used by your organization's own employees to manage the VRM process. Vendor Risk Manager (B), Vendor Risk Assessor (D), and Vendor Risk Reviewer (E) are all internal roles in the sn_vdr_risk_asmt scope. Vendor Contact (A) and Primary Vendor Contact (C) are external roles assigned to the vendor's representatives who access the Vendor Portal.

questions.stem: Roles preceded by sn_vdr_risk are for which scope?
questions.explanation: Roles with the sn_vdr_risk prefix belong to the GRC: Vendor Risk Core scope (B). This is distinct from sn_vdr_risk_asmt, which is the GRC: Vendor Risk Management scope used for assessment-related roles. GRC: Risk Management (C) uses the sn_risk prefix, and GRC: Vendor Risk Remediation (A) is a separate scope.

questions.stem: Before any changes to the configuration of an application are made, it is recommended that the correct update set and application scope are selected. What role is required for this functionality?

options.text: The Vendor Administrator role is required for this functionality
The Data Administrator role is required for this functionality
The User Administrator role is required for this functionality
The System Administrator role is required for this functionality

questions.explanation: The System Administrator role (admin) is required to select the correct update set and application scope before making configuration changes. This is a core platform administration function. Vendor Administrator, Data Administrator, and User Administrator are not standard roles that control update set or scope selection in ServiceNow.

questions.stem: What is the definition of ‘Risk Management’?

options.text: Policies/Standards/Procedures established to ensure an organization is aligned with corporate strategy and expectations are clearly defined
The process of conforming to standards, policies, and remediation of audit findings
The elimination of vulnerable surface area in an enterprise environment
Process to identify, assess, and respond to risks, threats and vulnerabilities that could compromise the business

questions.explanation: Risk Management is the process of identifying, assessing, and responding to risks, threats, and vulnerabilities that could compromise the business (D). Option A describes Governance (policies/standards/alignment). Option B describes Compliance (conforming to standards/remediation). Option C describes Vulnerability Management (eliminating vulnerable surface area).

questions.stem: Which of the following is the main benefit of using the Vendor Portal?

options.text: Assessments are performed via the Vendor Portal and spreadsheets
More efficiently communicating Assessments with a single contact
Assessments are shared through the Vendor Portal and email
More efficiently completing Assessments via the Vendor Portal

questions.explanation: The main benefit of the Vendor Portal is enabling vendors to more efficiently complete assessments directly through the portal (D). This centralizes the assessment workflow, eliminating the inefficiency of email-based and spreadsheet-based approaches. While the portal also supports communication, the primary value proposition is streamlined assessment completion.

questions.stem: Baseline email notifications that help to automate the vendor risk management process are installed with which plugin?
questions.explanation: Baseline email notifications for the vendor risk management process are installed with the GRC: Vendor Risk Management plugin (A). This plugin includes pre-configured notification templates that automate communications such as assessment reminders and issue alerts. The other GRC plugins (Audit, Risk, Policy/Compliance) handle notifications for their own respective processes.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the role assignment of vendor contacts in Vendor Risk Management?

options.text: When vendor contacts are created, they are automatically assigned the snc_internal role and the snc_external role
When vendor contacts are created, they must be manually assigned the snc_external role
When vendor contacts are created, they are automatically assigned the snc_internal role
When vendor contacts are created, they are automatically assigned the snc_external role

questions.explanation: When vendor contacts are created, they are automatically assigned the snc_external role (D). Contacts receive two roles automatically: vendor_contact (portal access) and snc_external (safeguard restricting access to the portal only, preventing unauthorized instance entry). They do NOT receive snc_internal, and the assignment is automatic, not manual.

questions.stem: What can a vendor contact do in the Vendor Portal? (Choose four.)

options.text: Communicate or share information with other vendors of the assessing organization
Create new issues and tasks for the vendor risk assessor team
Review and respond to issues created by the assessing organization
Manage vendor contacts and task assignments within the vendor organization
Respond to assessments sent by the assessing organization

questions.explanation: In the Vendor Portal, contacts can: update answers to returned questionnaires (A), review and respond to issues from the assessing organization (D), manage other vendor contacts and task assignments as primary contact (E), and respond to assessments sent by the assessing organization (F). Vendors cannot communicate with other vendors of the same assessing organization (B), and issues/tasks are created by assessors, not vendor contacts (C).

questions.stem: Which functions can be performed in the Vendor Portal? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The Vendor Portal supports three key functions: Assessment response (A) for completing questionnaires and document requests, Contact Management (B) for primary contacts to manage other vendor contacts, and Issue remediation (C) for reviewing and responding to issues raised by the assessing organization. The portal does not support scheduling web meetings (D) or virtual agent requests (E).

questions.stem: Where do vendors manage issues, respond to requests, and fulfill tasks assigned to them?
questions.explanation: Vendors manage issues, respond to requests, and fulfill tasks assigned to them through the Vendor Portal (B). The portal is the designated point of interaction between third parties and risk assessors, replacing inefficient spreadsheet-based and email workflows with a centralized online platform.

questions.stem: Which statements most accurately describe assignments to vendor contacts? (Choose two.)

options.text: Individual sections in the questionnaire or document request can be assigned
A questionnaire or document request cannot be assigned to multiple vendor contacts
A questionnaire can be read by vendor contacts that are not assigned
A questionnaire can only be completed by assigned vendor contacts

questions.explanation: Individual sections in a questionnaire or document request can be assigned to different vendor contacts (A), allowing work to be divided among multiple specialists. A questionnaire can only be completed by assigned vendor contacts (D), ensuring accountability. Questionnaires CAN be assigned to multiple contacts (B is wrong), and unassigned contacts typically cannot access the questionnaire (C is wrong).

questions.stem: What are the baseline mandatory fields when creating a new Vendor Contact? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The baseline mandatory fields when creating a new Vendor Contact are Name (First and Last) (A), Vendor (B), and Email (D). These are the minimum required fields to identify the contact, associate them with a vendor organization, and enable portal login/notifications. Department (C) and Role (E) are optional fields on the contact record.

questions.stem: Which of these options can be used in data cleansing when importing vendor data? (Choose three.)

options.text: Data Import or Data Source Transform

questions.explanation: When importing vendor data, three tools can be used for data cleansing: Field Normalization Rules (C) normalize field values automatically using declarative rules, Fix Scripts (D) allow scripted one-time data cleanup operations, and Data Import/Data Source Transforms (E) clean data during the import process via transform maps. Data Policies (A) are for validation, ACLs (B) handle security, and UI Policies (F) only affect the UI display.

questions.stem: Which of the following are functions of the Vendor Risk Assessor? (Choose three.)

options.text: Create a Primary Contact record for a Vendor

questions.explanation: The Vendor Risk Assessor can: access completed assessments from vendors (B), create issues for the vendor when non-compliance is found (D), and create a Primary Contact record for a Vendor to set up portal access (E). Assessors also manage contacts (create login, reset passwords, assign roles) and access completed assessments. Enabling cross-vendor communication (A) and updating contract deadlines (C) are not assessor functions.

questions.stem: What third-party vendor security evaluation solutions are commonly integrated with VRM out-of-the-box? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: ServiceNow VRM integrates out-of-the-box with two third-party vendor security evaluation solutions: Bitsight (C) and Security Scorecard (D). These platforms provide continuous external security monitoring and risk ratings that feed into the VRM risk assessment process. MyScoreMetrics (A) is not a recognized security evaluation product, and Vendor Insights (B) is not an OOB external integration.

questions.stem: What is the no code option to cleaning data being loaded into the Vendor Risk application?
questions.explanation: Field Normalization (B) is the no-code option for cleaning data loaded into the Vendor Risk application. It uses declarative rules to automatically normalize field values without requiring any scripting. Fix Scripts (A) require writing code. Import (C) is a data loading mechanism, not specifically a data cleaning tool.

questions.stem: When will the tiering value appear on the Vendor record?

options.text: When the Tiering Assessment record state is closed
When the Tiering Assessment record state is Tiering Assessment
When all tiering assessments have been completed

questions.explanation: The tiering value appears on the Vendor record when the Tiering Assessment record state is closed (A). Once the tiering assessment questionnaire is completed, scored, and the assessment record transitions to a closed state, the calculated tier value is written back to the vendor record. The value does not appear during an in-progress or open assessment state.

questions.stem: What can be used to automatically assign a Vendor tier value?
questions.explanation: A Tiering Assessment (C) is used to automatically assign a vendor tier value. The tiering assessment uses a questionnaire to evaluate the vendor based on criteria like data sensitivity, contract value, and business criticality. The vendor's responses are scored, and the resulting tier (Critical/High/Medium/Low) is automatically assigned to the vendor record upon assessment closure.

questions.stem: If clean data is not provided by the customer, what baseline solutions are available within the platform? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Baseline platform solutions for data cleansing include: Field normalization plugin (B) for declarative data normalization rules, System definition fix scripts module (D) for one-time scripted data cleanup, and System import transform map scripts (E) for cleaning data during import. Integration Hub ETL (A) is an add-on plugin, and Service Graph Connector (C) is specifically for CMDB discovery, not general data cleansing.

questions.stem: On the Contact record, there is a field for the Vendor name. This is which field (with a label change) from the sys_user table?
questions.explanation: The Vendor name field on the Contact record is the company field from the sys_user table with a changed label (C). In ServiceNow, the sys_user table has a reference field called 'company' that points to the core_company table. On vendor contact records, this field's label is changed to display 'Vendor' instead of 'Company,' linking the contact to their vendor organization.

questions.stem: The Template Designer is leveraged to create which of the following? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The Template Designer creates Document Request Templates (A) and Questionnaire Templates (D). The official description states: 'Use the Questionnaire Template Designer to create and edit questionnaire or document request templates.' Vendor Risk Assessments (C) are instances created from templates, not templates themselves. Assessment Template (B) is another name for the questionnaire template concept.

questions.stem: All Assessment Metrics within a Metric Category are scored, are rolled up, and get a score of.
questions.explanation: All Assessment Metrics within a Metric Category are scored, rolled up, and get a score of 0-100 (B). When the Scored option is selected, scoring uses a binary system of 0 or 100 reflecting correct/incorrect. When not scored, the calculation uses normalized values on a 0-100 scale through questionRating, questionPercentContribution, and questionNormalizedValue formulae.

questions.stem: The Template Designer contains which of the following elements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Option to create an Assessment Template and assign to a vendor
Properties for the supported question data types
Options to weight questions or sections
Design canvas for creating the questions and answers

questions.explanation: The Template Designer contains options to weight questions or sections (C) for adjusting the impact of different questions on the overall score, and a design canvas for creating questions and answers (D) where you drag controls to build the questionnaire. The designer also has Controls and Questions tabs, but the weighting and canvas are the two most distinctive architectural elements.

questions.stem: Where can the score for each Assessment Metric or Metric Category be configured?
questions.explanation: The score for each Assessment Metric or Metric Category is configured at the Assessment Metric Type record level (D). The Assessment Metric Type (AMT) record defines the overall scoring methodology, including whether metrics are scored using binary or scale-based methods. Individual metric scoring behavior is set via the Scored checkbox, but the overall configuration happens on the AMT record.

questions.stem: In order to evaluate a vendor on a recurring basis, configure a record in this table:
questions.explanation: To evaluate a vendor on a recurring basis, configure a record in the Repeating Assessments table (C). Navigate to All > TPRM > External Risk Assessments > Assessment scheduling, then create a new Repeating Assessment record with fields like assessment template, applies to (Third party/Engagement), and recurrence interval in months. This creates assessments automatically on a schedule.

questions.stem: A Document Request Template is a record in which table?
questions.explanation: A Document Request Template is a record in the Assessment metric type [asmt_metric_type] table (D). In VRM, both questionnaire templates and document request templates are stored as Assessment Metric Type records, differentiated by a type field. The AMT table serves as the unified storage for all template types used in the assessment framework.

questions.stem: From an Assessment record, the vendor risk assessor can click on “View Responses” to see which of the following?
questions.explanation: From an Assessment record, clicking 'View Responses' shows Assessment Responses (D). This displays the vendor's answers to the assessment questionnaire, including their selections, text responses, and any attached documentation. It does not show issue responses (A), email responses (B), or task responses (C).

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the SIG Lite?

options.text: The SIG Lite is a company specific questionnaire
The SIG Lite is a ServiceNow developed questionnaire
The SIG Lite assesses basic levels of due diligence and provides a broad but high-level understanding about internal security controls
The SIG Lite assesses service providers that store or manage highly sensitive or regulated information

questions.explanation: The SIG Lite (Standardized Information Gathering Lite) assesses basic levels of due diligence and provides a broad but high-level understanding about internal security controls (C). It is an industry-standard questionnaire created by the Shared Assessments organization, not a company-specific (A) or ServiceNow-developed (B) tool. The full SIG (not Lite) is used for highly sensitive/regulated information providers (D).

questions.stem: Which of the following statements are true about the Template Designer? (Choose two.)

options.text: Question weight can be set in the Template Designer
Correct answers can be set in the Template Designer
Questions can be mandatory in the Template Designer
Dependencies between questions cannot be set in the Template Designer
Questions cannot be mandatory in the Template Designer

questions.explanation: In the Template Designer, question weight can be set (A) to adjust how much each question contributes to the overall score, and correct answers can be set (B) using the Scored option which enables binary scoring (0 or 100) based on correct/incorrect answers. Dependencies between questions CAN be set (D is false). Questions CAN be made mandatory (E is false, C is true but not among the intended pair).

questions.stem: Which could have an impact on the vendor’s Risk Assessment rating? (Choose three.)

options.text: Answering one or more questions incorrectly
Reassigning a questionnaire to a contact

questions.explanation: Three factors can impact a vendor's Risk Assessment rating: answering one or more questions incorrectly (A) lowers the metric score, leaving answers blank (B) results in missing data that affects the overall assessment, and omitting documentation (C) in document requests impacts the completeness of the assessment. Spelling errors (D) do not affect automated scoring, and reassigning a questionnaire (E) is an administrative action with no scoring impact.

questions.stem: During the Generating Observations phase of the Vendor Risk Assessment, what action might be taken by the Risk Assessor?

options.text: Create issues from the assessment if necessary
Answer questions the vendor forgot to answer

questions.explanation: During the Generating Observations phase, the Risk Assessor reviews the vendor's responses and creates issues from the assessment if necessary (A). This phase is specifically designed for assessors to analyze responses, identify non-compliance or gaps, and generate formal issues that require vendor remediation. The assessor does not update scores directly (B), send emails (C), or answer on behalf of the vendor (D) during this phase.

questions.stem: For each questionnaire template/assessment metric type, how many vendor risk areas can be designated?
questions.explanation: For each questionnaire template or assessment metric type, only one vendor risk area can be designated (A). Each template is mapped to a single risk area (such as Information Security, Data Privacy, or Business Continuity) to ensure clear categorization of the assessment's focus. Multiple templates can cover different risk areas, but each individual template maps to exactly one.

questions.stem: To what type of assessment record can a vendor contact respond?
questions.explanation: Vendor contacts can respond to Vendor Risk Assessments (B) through the Vendor Portal. Tiering assessments (A) are typically internal evaluations completed by the assessing organization. Customer assessments (C) and external monitoring assessments (D) are not assessment types that vendor contacts directly respond to in the portal.

questions.stem: What are individual questions within a questionnaire or document request referred to as?
questions.explanation: Individual questions within a questionnaire or document request are referred to as Metrics (A), also called Assessment Metrics. Per the ServiceNow TPRM terminology table: 'Metric or Assessment metric — A single question within a questionnaire template.' Ratings (B), Templates (C), and Tiers (D) refer to different concepts in the VRM framework.

questions.stem: In addition to the “Design canvas”, which elements does the Template Designer contain? (Choose three.)

options.text: Header bar which contains tabs that display different view and a menu of various functions
Controls for the supported question data types
Question and Categories tabs that contain question/categories that were added to the Question Bank
Risk criteria to identity conditions and risk areas

questions.explanation: The Template Designer contains, in addition to the design canvas: a header bar with tabs displaying different views and a menu of functions (A) including Save, Preview, New Assessment, Load Assessment, and Copy Assessment; Controls for supported question data types (B) like Choice, Scale, String, Boolean, Attachment, etc.; and Question and Categories tabs containing items from the Question Bank (D). FAQ Page/Tour (C) is a portal feature, not a designer element. Risk criteria (E) is not part of the Template Designer UI.

questions.stem: In the baseline, what component sends reminder notifications about assessments?

options.text: Events fired by a Business Rule

questions.explanation: In the baseline VRM configuration, reminder notifications about assessments are sent by a Scheduled Job (C). The scheduled job periodically checks for pending or overdue assessments and triggers email reminders automatically. This is not an on-demand process (A), nor is it driven by Business Rule events (B) or Workflows (D) in the baseline configuration.

questions.stem: Vendor Risk Tasks are saved to which one of the following tables?
questions.explanation: Vendor Risk Tasks are saved to the [sn_vdr_risk_asmt_task] table (D). This table follows the VRM naming convention using the sn_vdr_risk_asmt scope prefix. While it extends the base [task] table (A), the specific table for VRM tasks is sn_vdr_risk_asmt_task. Tables like [planned_task] (B) and [sn_vendor_risk_task] (C) are not the correct VRM task tables.

questions.stem: What is the minimum role required to create a new Vendor Risk Issue?
questions.explanation: The minimum role required to create a new Vendor Risk Issue is the Vendor Risk Assessor role [sn_vdr_risk_asmt.vendor_assessor] (A). Assessors review vendor responses during the assessment process and create issues when non-compliance or gaps are identified. The Reviewer role (B) has more limited permissions, while the Manager role (C) and admin (D) have higher privileges than the minimum needed.

questions.stem: What are the features of Vendor Risk Issues? (Choose two.)

options.text: Generate audit tasks for the vendor risk team
Can only be seen by the customer’s vendor risk team
Provide vendor direct access to update and respond to Issues
Can be generated on-demand or automatically due to an incorrect answer

questions.explanation: Vendor Risk Issues have two key features: they provide vendor direct access to update and respond to issues through the Vendor Portal (C), and they can be generated on-demand by assessors or automatically due to an incorrect answer via issue generation rules (D). Issues are NOT limited to only the customer's team (B is wrong — they can be visible in the portal). They do not generate audit tasks (A) — they generate remediation tasks.

questions.stem: Vendor Risk Issues are usually created in which stage of an Assessment?
questions.explanation: Vendor Risk Issues are usually created during the Generating Observations stage (B) of an assessment. In this stage, the risk assessor reviews the vendor's submitted responses, identifies areas of non-compliance or concern, and creates issues that require vendor remediation. This happens after Responses Received (A) and before Finalizing with Vendor (D).

questions.stem: A Vendor Risk Task can be created from which of the following records?
questions.explanation: A Vendor Risk Task can be created from three types of records: Vendor Risk Issue, Assessment, and Vendor (D). Tasks can be generated from issues to track specific remediation activities, from assessments to assign follow-up work, and from the vendor record itself to track vendor-level activities. Policy records (A, B, C) and Risk records (B) are GRC entities, not direct VRM task creation sources.

questions.stem: What are some of the purposes of a Vendor Risk Issue? (Choose two.)

options.text: Log access-related incidents for the vendor portal
Indicate vendors that need further assessment
Accept risks identified in the assessment

questions.explanation: Vendor Risk Issues serve two main purposes: indicating vendors that need further assessment or attention (B) by flagging areas of concern identified during the assessment process, and tracking remediation of compliance gaps (D) by creating a formal record of what needs to be fixed and monitoring resolution progress. Logging access incidents (A) is for security incident management, and accepting risk (C) is handled through risk acceptance workflows.

questions.stem: The VRM issue management process is frequently unique to an organization. What two ServiceNow provided building blocks were covered in this course to help with customer needs that might arise during the lifecycle of VRM issues? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The VRM issue management lifecycle can be customized using two ServiceNow automation building blocks: Flow Designer (A) for modern, no-code/low-code automation, and Workflow Editor (C) for legacy workflow automation. Both platforms can be used to define approval processes, escalation paths, and automated actions throughout the issue lifecycle. Service Management (B) and Incident Management (D) are separate application areas, not building blocks.

questions.stem: In the Vendor Portal, who can reassign Assessments?
questions.explanation: In the Vendor Portal, the Primary Contact (C) can reassign assessments to other vendor contacts. Primary contacts can 'delegate questionnaires, tasks, and issues to other third-party contacts' and manage contact assignments within the vendor organization. Vendor Business Owner (A), Vendor (B), and Vendor Manager (D) are not portal roles with reassignment capability.

questions.stem: A Vendor Risk Assessment that consists of a SIG Lite questionnaire and two document requests are displayed as how many total requests in the Vendor Portal?
questions.explanation: A Vendor Risk Assessment consisting of a SIG Lite questionnaire and two document requests displays as 3 total requests in the Vendor Portal (B). Each component — the SIG Lite questionnaire (1) and each document request (2) — appears as a separate request that can be individually assigned to different vendor contacts and tracked independently.

questions.stem: When an assessor creates an issue or task from the vendor record, it is grouped with other issues or tasks for what ServiceNow entity?
questions.explanation: When an assessor creates an issue or task from the vendor record, it is grouped with other issues or tasks for that specific Vendor (A). This vendor-centric grouping allows all risk issues and remediation tasks to be managed and tracked at the vendor level, providing a consolidated view of all outstanding items for a single vendor entity.

questions.stem: Who is able to change the password for the vendor contact? (Choose two.)

options.text: Vendor contact via the Forgot Password link

questions.explanation: Two parties can change the password for a vendor contact: the system administrator (sys_admin) (B) who can reset any user's password, and the vendor contact themselves via the Forgot Password link (C) on the portal login page. Secondary contacts can 'Change a password or request a new password' in the Vendor Portal. The Vendor Contract Relationship Manager (A) and Vendor Risk Reviewer (D) do not have password reset privileges.

questions.stem: Which statement accurately describes the visibility and audit history of actions and communications in the Vendor Risk Management application?

options.text: The vendor and assessor interactions are captured in the Vendor Risk Issue record and are only visible from the portal view
The Vendor Risk Issues created and the activity and history are lost from the Vendor Assessment Portal when the associated vendor contact changes
The Vendor Risk Issues created and the activity and history will remain in the Vendor Assessment Portal even when vendor contacts change
The vendor and assessor interactions are captured in the Vendor Risk Issue record and are only visible from the platform view

questions.explanation: In the Vendor Risk Management application, Vendor Risk Issues and their associated activity and history are persistent records in the platform. They remain in the Vendor Assessment Portal even when vendor contacts change. The records are tied to the vendor entity, not to individual contacts. When a contact is updated or replaced, the historical interaction data (issues, communications, audit trail) is preserved. Options A and D are incorrect because interactions are visible from both portal and platform views, not limited to one.

questions.stem: The assessment page provides an area to import what kind of a completed questionnaire?
questions.explanation: The assessment page provides an area to import a completed SIG (Standardized Information Gathering) questionnaire (C). Third parties can use the SIG questionnaire to provide assessment documentation, uploading a pre-filled SIG spreadsheet or responding to a form-based questionnaire imported to the instance. GDPR (A), SOC1/SOC2 (B), and SOX (D) are compliance frameworks, not importable questionnaire formats in VRM.

questions.stem: How are Vendor Risk questionnaires and document requests displayed on the Vendor Portal?

options.text: As separate requests and can be assigned to different vendor contacts
As separate requests and can only be assigned to the same vendor contact
As a single assessment assigned to a single vendor contact
As a single assessment assigned to a single engagement contact

questions.explanation: Vendor Risk questionnaires and document requests are displayed on the Vendor Portal as separate requests and can be assigned to different vendor contacts (A). Each component of an assessment (questionnaires and document requests) appears independently in the portal, allowing the primary contact to delegate individual components to the most appropriate specialist within the vendor organization.

questions.stem: In the Paris release and beyond, the scoped vendor portal (svdp) will be installed by default but can be overridden in which System Property record to use the legacy/traditional vendor portal (vdp)?
questions.explanation: The system property sn_vdr_risk_asmt.vendor_portal_endpoint (C) controls which vendor portal endpoint is used. From the Paris release onward, the scoped vendor portal (svdp) is installed by default, but this property can be overridden to point to the legacy/traditional vendor portal (vdp) if needed. The scoped prefix variants (B, D) and the base property without endpoint (A) are not the correct property names.

questions.stem: Which of these must be true in order for a vendor risk issue to be visible in the Vendor Portal?

options.text: There must be at least one secondary contact for the vendor
The primary vendor contact must have the sn_vdr_issues role
Issues are always visible in the vendor portal
The Visible in vendor portal field must have a value of true

questions.explanation: For a vendor risk issue to be visible in the Vendor Portal, the 'Visible in vendor portal' field must have a value of true (D). This boolean field on the issue record explicitly controls portal visibility. Issues are NOT always visible (C is wrong). While the primary contact exists (A), their presence alone doesn't determine issue visibility. The sn_vdr_issues role (B) is not what controls this — the field value does.

questions.stem: Which GRC records can be related to an Entity? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: In the GRC framework, three types of records can be related to an Entity: Risks (C) representing threats to the entity, Policies (D) governing the entity's operations, and Controls (E) mitigating the entity's risks. Entity Types (A) define what type an entity is (not a related record), and Vendors (B) are themselves entities rather than records related to other entities.

questions.stem: A vendor is assessed and responds to a question which impacts one of the Controls applied to them. When is the Control Status updated?

options.text: When the Vendor Risk Assessment State is Responses Received
When the Vendor Risk Assessment State is Finalizing with Vendor or Closed
When the Vendor Risk Assessment response is saved
When all Questions in the Vendor Risk Assessment have a response

questions.explanation: The Control Status is updated when the Vendor Risk Assessment state is Finalizing with Vendor or Closed (B). Assessment responses are reviewed and finalized before control statuses are recalculated. Updating during Responses Received (A) would be premature since the assessor hasn't reviewed the responses yet. Individual response saves (C) and completion of all questions (D) don't trigger control status updates.

questions.stem: What is the advantage of using both VRM and GRC/IRM?

options.text: Vendor Risk engagements automatically match with Audit engagements
All compliance controls are automatically visible to the vendor risk manage
Primary vendor contacts can then see their overall non compliant risk score
Non compliant controls automatically adjust the risk score for a vendor entity

questions.explanation: The advantage of using both VRM and GRC/IRM together is that non-compliant controls automatically adjust the risk score for a vendor entity (D). When assessment responses reveal control deficiencies, the integrated risk framework automatically recalculates the vendor's overall risk score. This provides a real-time, holistic view of vendor risk that combines assessment results with control compliance status.

questions.stem: On which of the following tables can you create vendor risk reports? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Vendor risk reports can be created on three key tables: Company [core_company] (A) for vendor-level data including tiers and classifications, Vendor Risk Assessment [sn_vdr_risk_asmt_assessment] (B) for assessment scores and status data, and Vendor Risk Issue [sn_vdr_risk_asmt_issue] (C) for tracking remediation and compliance gaps. Vendor Contact (D) and Vendor Activity (E) tables are less commonly used for risk reporting.

questions.stem: A Vendor Risk Manager needs to run a report displaying Critical Vendors. On which table would this person run a report?
questions.explanation: To run a report displaying Critical Vendors, the Vendor Risk Manager would use the Company [core_company] table (A). The vendor tier designation (Critical/High/Medium/Low) is stored as a field on the Company record. Filtering the Company table where vendor=true and tier=Critical produces the desired report. The other tables track assessments (D), issues (B), or contacts (C), not vendor criticality levels.

questions.stem: Key data sources for Vendor Risk reporting include which of the following tables? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The two key data sources for Vendor Risk reporting are the Vendor Risk Assessment [sn_vdr_risk_asmt_assessment] table (A) containing assessment scores, statuses, and compliance data, and the Vendor Risk Issue [sn_vdr_risk_asmt_issue] table (E) containing remediation tracking and compliance gap data. Questionnaire Templates (B) are design-time records, Benchmark Scores (C) are not a primary reporting table, and Survey Scores (D) relate to a different ServiceNow module.
